text:
Sara: Quick async from my shift — handoff notes:
- Two alerts flapped on kv-cache writes between 03:10-03:25 UTC.
- I followed the SLO-flap runbook and rotated the eviction policy, restarted the cache deployment:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/kv-cache
```
- Suppression window applied for 20m. SLO impact: 24h = 99.92% (target 99.9%) — looking fine but want a follow-up on root cause.
- Leaving ticket: infra#789 (will add logs + timeline).

Raj: thanks — can you confirm the exact check you hit? was it high-5xx rate or latency breaches?

Sara: It was elevated 5xx for the write-path
- spike in write latency -> transient retry loop
- logs show a pattern around shard-3 garbage collection

Amy: I can take infra#789 and do a deeper dig in the morning. I'll check shard-3 metrics and storage IO.
Will also open a quick PR if we need a backoff tweak. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Alert suppression created by @Sara for alert "kv-cache-write-5xx" until 2026-03-17T03:40:00Z. Incident ID: ib-2026-0317-22

Ethan: re: backoff — we should consider jittered retry and a small circuit-breaker. Quick grep to get logs:
```
journalctl -u kv-cache | grep "shard-3" | tail -n 200
```
Also opened infra PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2345 — tagging Amy.

Amy: ack, will start with the GC profiles and disk IO. If I see any persistent error rates >0.2% sustained, I'll escalate to oncall for a canary rollback. :eyes:

Sara: thanks team. No blocking items from my side. Leaving the follow-ups to Amy/Ethan. I'll update the ticket and attach the runbook steps and the restart command output.

Raj: great. If anything needs urgent paging overnight, mention @oncall in the thread. Otherwise we'll review during morning sync.

Sara: noted. good night :zzz:
